clue.text: Shy, though sounds belligerent?

definitions.meaning: timid and easily embarrassed in company
split as ..., the word seems to mean full of bashing, i.e. spoiling for a fight

explanation.surface: Someone timid whose voice nonetheless comes across as aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: the word looks and sounds like 'full of bashes', though it means the opposite of aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shy and being bashful are synonyms for diffident, self-conscious behaviour.

clue.text: Don't allow the Church to take a dodgy loan in Spain

parts.note: to bar is to forbid
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters of loan are shuffled

explanation.surface: Forbidding the Church from taking out a shady loan in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' shuffles the loan's letters; the definition is only 'in Spain', standing for a city there, so the clue reads as one sentence about a banking scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a major Catalan city on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: He learns a medical specialism under the boss

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another comes below it

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: A trainee doctor studying a specialty under a senior consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not the manager but a stud or knob, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is one who is studying, a learner.

clue.text: Mercenary used to get fish in the country

indicators.note: the fish is placed in the country

parts.note: France is a country
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A soldier for hire was used to catching fish in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance was originally a medieval hired soldier, a mercenary.

clue.text: Gait is uneven but not stiff

definitions.meaning: a lame, halting way of walking

explanation.surface: A walk that lurches but is not rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbling walk and a floppy state are both senses of the word.

clue.text: See many a delinquent lad placed here

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a rowdy youth of 1950s Britain

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at where a young offender has been put.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth cult associated with drape jackets and street trouble; 'here' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something located has been situated or set in a particular spot.

clue.text: He is qualified to dispense a centilitre right away

indicators.note: dispensing the liquid scatters the letters
the letter for right is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A pharmacist licensed to measure out a centilitre immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from A CENTILITRE, and 'dispense' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A licentiate holds a licence to practise a profession, such as medicine.

clue.text: Younger son Edward and Bill raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the whole is reversed

parts.note: Ted is short for Edward
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A family's junior boy with Edward and Bill brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TED plus AC upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is historically a younger son of a noble family.

clue.text: Touching point for a brown man

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
gent is a man

explanation.surface: Asking a tanned man to make a moving point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks emotional, but it means in contact, as a tangent touches a curve at one point.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent meets a curve at a single point of contact.

clue.text: Play daughter to god?

parts.note: Rama is a Hindu god

explanation.surface: A drama whose plot sends a girl to a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a stage play.

clue.text: Powder for a blusher?

parts.note: reads like a remedy for someone who goes red easily, but describes cosmetic powder that gives the cheeks colour

explanation.surface: A shy person who blushes is offered some powder to cover it.
explanation.walkthrough: A blusher is both a person who reddens and a cheek cosmetic; the powder makes you look flushed rather than hiding a flush.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is a red cosmetic powder applied to colour the cheeks.

clue.text: Did the' original Diana come from this old kingdom?

indicators.note: the original form of the words is taken to be a scrambled version of the place name

explanation.surface: A question whether the first Diana, the goddess, hailed from an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' asks for the letters of DIANA COME to be put back in their original order, giving the ancient kingdom of Philip and Alexander.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia was an ancient Greek kingdom, home of Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Smoothly accommodating the archdeacon in the diocese

indicators.note: the diocese takes in the archdeacon, giving him a place within it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman settled into his diocese without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: An Anglican archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven; Ely is the crossword's favourite diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something smoothly is to do it steadily and without unevenness.

clue.text: He's hated writing three articles about those people

indicators.note: the articles are written around the people, enclosing them

parts.note: an, a and a are three indefinite articles
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A loathed man composing three pieces of journalism on certain folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' just sets the scene: the three articles are not news pieces but the grammatical words AN, A, A, placed about THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a person or thing detested or cursed.

clue.text: Sad arrest of such a worker

parts.note: blue means sad
to collar someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A gloomy arrest of a manual labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar describes manual or industrial workers and their jobs.

clue.text: Frequently decimal

definitions.meaning: split as ..., which is what decimal means: based on tens

explanation.surface: Two words loosely about how often numbers come in tens.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently and repeatedly describe something happening many times; decimal counting goes in tens.

clue.text: Dudley or some other place

definitions.meaning: Robert Dudley, favourite of Elizabeth I
an English Midlands city, in contrast to Dudley, also a Midlands town

explanation.surface: Choosing between Dudley or some other town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley looks like the West Midlands town, but it is Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's courtier, whose title was Earl of Leicester; LEICESTER is also an East Midlands city.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley held the earldom named after that city, which is a separate Midlands place.

clue.text: Change wheels before you get abroad

indicators.note: changing the wheels rearranges the word

parts.note: ere means before

explanation.surface: Swapping a car's wheels before going overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' turns WHEELS into ELSEWH.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means away in another place.

clue.text: Thought man rude, it could be

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: Someone considered a man impolite, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ruminated is to have pondered or reflected.

clue.text: Settlement for eastern people in great ferment

indicators.note: eastern people are placed inside the stirred-up letters
in ferment means agitated, so the word great is churned up

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: A deal being sought for oriental peoples amid great unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferment' gives AGRET, and 'in' sets the eastern people inside that jumble; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement between parties is an accord they have reached.

clue.text: Went to Monte Carlo, maybe, and got better

definitions.meaning: took part in a motor rally such as the Monte Carlo Rally

explanation.surface: A driver who competed at Monaco and recovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing in a motor rally and recovering from illness are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Crowd start to swig cordial

indicators.note: the start of the word swig supplies its opening letter

parts.note: cordial means warm and friendly

explanation.surface: A crowd begins to drink a fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like a drink to swig, but it is the adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large, dense mass of people or insects.

clue.text: Talk giving publicity to women's wear

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is publicity
a dress is worn by women

explanation.surface: A speech promoting women's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech.

clue.text: Sailor sends first trade union apprentice back for the washing

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: sends back means the following pieces are returned in reverse order

parts.note: No. 1 means first, written NOI
L for learner stands for an apprentice

explanation.surface: A seaman orders the first union trainee home to do the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the run after the sailor, giving LUTION; 'first' is No. 1, written as the letters N, O and the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablution is a formal word for the act of washing oneself.

clue.text: Expert has characters taped

indicators.note: has the characters, that is the letters, of the word taped in another order

explanation.surface: A specialist's personality is recorded on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a highly skilled person.

clue.text: Add on nearly everything to get the sum

parts.note: to tot up is to add

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Adding up almost everything to reach the final figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last L of ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the sum of figures.

clue.text: Country garden on Dartmoor, say

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: Dartmoor, a moorland in Devon, is in South-West England, abbreviated SW
Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: A rural garden laid out on a Devon moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country garden' reads as a cottage garden, but Country is the definition; Dartmoor is a moor in Devon, in England's south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: Disease said to take hold

indicators.note: said indicates that the word for the disease is spoken

parts.note: grippe is an old name for influenza

explanation.surface: An illness that is said to take hold of you.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIPPE is a dated French-derived word for flu.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip is to grasp firmly.

clue.text: Paul, for example, always carries a gun

indicators.note: the word for always holds the gun inside it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a pistol is a handgun

explanation.surface: Saint Paul, or someone like him, never goes out unarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic form of ever; Paul is the apostle who wrote the New Testament letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistoler writes or reads epistles, and the apostle Paul wrote many New Testament letters.

clue.text: Is the lady right to turn things inside out?

parts.note: Eve is the first lady of Genesis

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman is entitled to turn everything upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lady' points to Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert something is to turn it outward, as a sleeve is pulled out the wrong way.

clue.text: Doorkeeper lets in a divine little chap

indicators.note: the doorkeeper admits the divine, who goes inside

parts.note: a tiler is the doorkeeper of a Masonic lodge
DD, Doctor of Divinity, denotes a divine or clergyman

explanation.surface: A porter admits a small clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Freemasonry the tiler guards the lodge door; DD is the degree Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is British slang for a small child or anything tiny.

clue.text: Insisted on being given the iron treatment

definitions.meaning: smoothed with a hot iron, as clothes are

explanation.surface: Someone who stood firm while being ironed.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to urge firmly, and clothes smoothed with an iron have been flattened.
